newsitem.title: GREECE: EMERGING MKT BOND ISSUANCE UP 46PCT IN H1- SALOMON.
newsitem.headline: EMERGING MKT BOND ISSUANCE UP 46PCT IN H1- SALOMON.

text.p: Emerging market bond issuance in
international capital markets climbed to a new record in the
first half of 1997 as Eurobond and foreign bond issue volume
advanced to $63.2 billion -- a 46 percent pickup over a year
earlier, said Salomon Brothers.
"Low interest rates in the industrialised countries
continued to provide favourable financing terms for emerging
market borrowers in the first half of 1997," notes analyst
Rosario Benavides in Salomon's global fixed income review.
"The volume of placements in the first half dwarfed the
second-highest emerging market issuance record set in 1993."
The borrowing bonanza was underpinned by the decline if
international interest rates in most industrialised countries
and flatter yield curves which provided emerging market
borrowers with an attractive primary market.
Thus, the tally of total emerging market international bonds
outstanding -- excluding Brady bonds -- reached about $320
billion at end-June 1997.
Latin American and Asian borrowers accounted for 39.1
percent and 38.4 percent of the market, respectively, while east
and southeast European issuers captured an 18.9 percent share.
The remaining 3.4 percent belonged to African and Middle East
borrowers.
"The resurgence of U.S. $-denominated issuance which began
last year continued well into 1997, reflecting a relative
strengthening of the U.S. dollar against other currencies and
the consequent keen investor demand for $-denominated assets,"
Benavides said.
Nonetheless, several borrowers that already launched
benchmarks in the Eurodollar or Yankee markets have launched
inaugural issues in other currencies like the mark and the yen
in order to establish investor bases in other regions and
diversify their funding sources.
According to Salomon, refinancing needs for maturing debt
this year will keep emerging market borrowers active in the
primary market as some $31 billion in international bonds will
mature in 1997 -- $36 billion next year.
Most borrowers raising capital in international bond markets
-- the gamut covers a wide spectrum -- aim to extend the
maturity profile of their flotations and smooth out the
amortisation schedule of their debt, especially those facing
large redemptions in 1997 and 1998.
In addition, borrowers seek to trim overall financing costs,
refinance old debt at lower costs and establish benchmarks in
different currency markets, paving the way for future corporate
issuance and widening their investor base, Salomon said.
East and southeast European borrowers issued $9.7 billion in
international capital markets in the first half of 1997,
garnering 15.4 percent of total new issue volume, 2.1 percent
higher than a year earlier and 3.6 percent above their share for
the entire 1996.
"Issuance in June alone accounted for almost 49 percent of
issuance for the region and mainly reflected new borrowers in
the market -- the composition changing dramatically," Salomon
said.
More than 41 percent of new issue volume during the
comparable year-earlier period was launched by the Hellenic
Republic. But this year, Greece was absent from the market until
the last day of June when it launched two deutsche
mark-denominated 100 million FRNs.
